_comment: Corpus for the confusable-host rule (src/confusable-host.mjs). SINGLE SOURCE: every test that scores the rule, and any external benchmark harness, reads this file rather than restating cases. `benign` is the half that decides whether the rule is honest — real internationalized domain labels across many scripts, every one of which must produce ZERO findings; a rule that flags one of these is trading a real false positive for recall. `attacks` carries the expected severity per label, and the two tiers are evidential strength rather than attack class: `warning` for a label whose whole TR39 skeleton is pure ASCII, so it reads as an ASCII name outright, and `note` for a label that carries a cross-script confusable but keeps an unmapped glyph, so it reads as no ASCII name — thin evidence, since an ordinary word with one look-alike letter produces the same shape. `misses` are vectors the rule does NOT catch, kept here so the residual is a tested fact rather than a claim in a doc.

benign.label: istanbul
benign.note: pure ASCII is never a pretender

attacks.label: раураӏ
attacks.note: every letter is Cyrillic, yet the whole label skeletons to ASCII

attacks.label: аppleм
attacks.note: unmapped м suppresses the strong rule, leaving the quiet mixed-script tier

misses.label: мicrosoft
misses.why: Cyrillic м has no TR39 ASCII mapping, so the skeleton keeps it (мicrosoft) and the label reads as no ASCII name. The mixed-script tier misses it too: that tier fires on a confusable glyph sitting among Latin letters, and м is not a confusable at all, so the label carries no finding to mark.

misses.label: αρριε
misses.why: Greek ε has no TR39 mapping to Latin e, so the skeleton keeps it (appiε) and the label is not claiming to be an ASCII name. Single-script, so no mixed-script note either.

misses.label: paypaI
misses.why: ASCII-only lookalike (capital I for lowercase l). Declared out of scope: skeleton('paypaI') is 'paypai', and flagging I-versus-l in general text is a precision catastrophe.

misses.label: rnicrosoft
misses.why: ASCII-only lookalike (rn for m). Same out-of-scope class as paypaI.
